title: Fraïssé limits: constructing a homogeneous countable structure

based_on.title: Lecture Notes: An Introduction to Model Theory

summary: Schedule every finite extension request to construct a countable limit, then prove its universality, symmetry and uniqueness.
abstract: A collection of finite structures may be the age of many different countable structures. Can one arrange that every permitted finite extension can be placed around a copy already chosen? Amalgamation makes each such request possible, and successive finite batches ensure that all requests are eventually answered. Their union is a Fraïssé limit: it has exactly the prescribed finite pieces, and every isomorphism between its finite pieces extends to a symmetry of the whole structure. A back-and-forth argument proves uniqueness while preserving any specified finite match, and a one-sided construction embeds every compatible countable structure into the limit. The limit is countably infinite exactly when the class contains arbitrarily large finite structures; bounded classes can have finite limits.
